title: The Goddess in all beings
hook: a red book read aloud before sunrise for nine mornings, and the hymn at its heart: the Goddess in all beings
carry: shakti: the goddess lives in all beings as power
tomorrow: Kanya puja: girls as the Goddess

segments.voice: Yesterday, Holi in the morning: Krishna, Radha, and a pinch of color. Your line: lila. God plays, and love plays back.
screen: `HOLI: GOD PLAYS, AND LOVE PLAYS BACK.`

segments.voice: Before sunrise, in a small kitchen in Kolkata, a grandmother sits on a low stool with a red cloth-bound book open on her knees. She reads aloud in Sanskrit, fast and steady, the way you read something you've read every autumn of your life. A lamp burns beside her. She'll do this every morning until the ninth. Inside are the battles you heard on day eighty-seven. But today, one hymn from the middle of the book, sung by gods who had lost everything.
screen: `BEFORE SUNRISE, A RED BOOK.` → `READ ALOUD, NINE MORNINGS.` → `ONE HYMN AT ITS HEART.`

segments.voice: The book is the Devi Mahatmya, the Glory of the Goddess. Many families read it, or have a priest read it, across the nine nights; it also goes by Durga Saptashati, the seven hundred, after its traditional count of verses. It tells three battles, and in the third there's a scene. Two demon brothers, Shumbha and Nishumbha, have taken heaven. The gods, thrown out, climb into the Himalaya and do the only thing left: they praise the Goddess. Their hymn is one of the most loved in Hinduism. Line after line, they bow to the Goddess who lives in all beings: as consciousness, as sleep, as hunger, as strength, as patience, as faith, as compassion, as mother. And every line ends the same way: we bow to her, we bow to her, again and again. Just then Parvati comes down to bathe in the river. Whom are you praising? she asks. And out of her own body steps another goddess, shining, who answers: they're praising me. Then she goes out to meet the brothers. Here's the teaching under the festival. The Goddess is Shakti, power itself: not only a figure riding a lion, but the strength inside every living thing, even sleep, hunger, a mother's care. That's why the nights are kept for nine forms, the Navadurga, one each night, from Shailaputri, daughter of the mountain, to Siddhidatri, who gives perfection. Many families greet her with Jai Mata Di, victory to the Mother. The same power, nine faces, and the same power in the people in your own house.
screen: `THE DEVI MAHATMYA, READ ALOUD.` · `THE GODS' HYMN: IN ALL BEINGS.` · `WE BOW TO HER, AGAIN AND AGAIN.` · `SHAKTI: POWER ITSELF.` · then, large: `THE SAME POWER, NINE FACES.`

segments.voice: Sit with the lamp, the way the grandmother does. If you pray, say Jai Mata Di softly, or the hymn's refrain: we bow to her, again and again. Then think of the strength in one ordinary person near you: a grandmother's patience, a friend's nerve, your own tired body still going. In Navaratri's eyes, that's her. Bow to it inside. If you don't pray, simply notice it, and be grateful for it.
Navaratri. Nine nights of the Goddess, kept with her book read aloud and one of her nine forms honored each night.
Your line: shakti. The Goddess lives in all beings as power. That's day one hundred forty-three.

screen: `SHAKTI: THE GODDESS LIVES IN ALL BEINGS AS POWER.` → `DAY 143 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: KANYA PUJA.`

howItsDone: During Navaratri many Hindus read or recite the Devi Mahatmya (the Durga Saptashati) across the nine nights and honor the Goddess in nine forms, the Navadurga, one each night, with fasting and prayers; the tenth day, Vijayadashami or Dussehra, celebrates victory.

what a scholar hears: in the Devi Mahatmya's fifth chapter the gods' hymn bows to the Devi who abides in all beings (ya devi sarvabhuteshu…), and the Goddess emerges from Parvati's body; the text sits inside the Markandeya Purana and is recited as the Durga Saptashati or Chandi Path.

Devi Mahatmya.meaning: the Glory of the Goddess, a Sanskrit text read across Navaratri

Markandeya Purana.meaning: the old Sanskrit collection the Devi Mahatmya is set inside

Navadurga.meaning: the Goddess in nine forms, one honored each night

Kali.meaning: the dark, fierce form who springs from the Goddess's brow

Shumbha.meaning: one of two demon brothers in the third battle

Shakti.meaning: power: the Goddess as the strength in every being

Jai Mata Di.meaning: victory to the Mother: a common Navaratri greeting

notes: Devi Mahatmya: 'Saptashati, the seven hundred, after its traditional count of verses'; chapters 81–93 of the Markandeya Purana in the common numbering. Confirm.
Recitation of the Devi Mahatmya across Navaratri (whole or in parts, at home or by a priest) varies by region and family. Confirm.

Navadurga order and one-line glosses (Shailaputri, Brahmacharini, Chandraghanta, Kushmanda, Skandamata, Katyayani, Kalaratri, Mahagauri, Siddhidatri) follow the common list (e.g. Devi Kavacham). Confirm.
Kali springs from Ambika's brow in Devi Mahatmya ch. 7 (against Chanda and Munda); the promise to return when called is paraphrased from chs. 4 and 11. Confirm.
The hook's Kolkata grandmother is an illustrative scene, not a claim.
